stem: The student wants to describe the method Sayegh's team used to date the lower hearth. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Tell Qarsa, an archaeological site in northern Jordan, contains two ancient hearths, one buried below the other.
• In 1998, Nadia Haddad's team dated both hearths by comparing pottery found in them with pottery of known age.
• In 2019, a team led by Omar Sayegh returned to the site.
• Sayegh's team dated the upper hearth by radiocarbon analysis of charred barley seeds found in it.
• The lower hearth held no seeds, so the team measured the light released by heated quartz grains from its clay.
• The lower hearth proved to be about 5,200 years old, older than earlier estimates.
choices: To date Tell Qarsa's lower hearth, Haddad's team compared the pottery found in it with pottery of known age.
Sayegh's team dated Tell Qarsa's upper hearth by performing radiocarbon analysis on charred barley seeds found in it.
Sayegh's team found that Tell Qarsa's lower hearth was about 5,200 years old, older than earlier estimates had suggested.
Sayegh's team dated Tell Qarsa's lower hearth by measuring the light released by heated quartz grains from its clay.
explanation: The goal has three restrictions that must all hold: Sayegh's team (not Haddad's), the lower hearth (not the upper one), and the method (not the result). Choice D is the only sentence whose main clause meets all three. It names Sayegh's team, the lower hearth, and the technique they used: measuring light from heated quartz grains.

A.why: You matched 'lower hearth' and 'method' but missed which team the goal names. This is the 1998 pottery comparison by Haddad's team, not Sayegh's method.

B.why: You matched Sayegh's team and a dating method, but this method was used on the upper hearth. The goal restricts you to the lower one, which had no seeds to radiocarbon-date.

C.why: You got the right team and the right hearth and stopped there. This sentence gives the finding (the age), but the goal asks how the hearth was dated, which is the method stage of the notes, not the result.

stem: The student wants to describe the effect cereal rye had on corn yield during the drought year. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Agronomist Lucía Ferreyra studied whether winter cover crops affect the yield of corn planted after them.
• In Nebraska plots sown the previous winter with cereal rye, crimson clover, or nothing, she grew corn in 2021 and 2022.
• 2021 was unusually wet; 2022 was a drought year.
• In 2021, corn after rye yielded 4% less than corn in bare plots.
• In 2022, corn after rye yielded 17% more than corn in bare plots.
• Rye residue likely helped the soil hold moisture.
• In 2022, corn after clover yielded 6% more than corn in bare plots.
choices: In 2021, an unusually wet year, corn planted after cereal rye yielded 4% less than corn planted in bare plots.
In 2022, a drought year, corn planted after cereal rye yielded 17% more than corn planted in bare plots.
In 2022, a drought year, residue left by cereal rye likely helped Ferreyra's plots hold moisture in the soil.
In 2022, a drought year, corn planted after crimson clover yielded 6% more than corn planted in bare plots.
explanation: The goal sets three conditions: the crop has to be cereal rye, the year has to be the drought year (2022), and the sentence has to state the effect on corn yield. Choice B is the only one that meets all three. It reports that corn after rye yielded 17% more than corn in bare plots in 2022.

A.why: You found rye's effect on yield but took it from the wrong year. 2021 was the wet year, and the goal restricts you to the drought.

C.why: You matched rye and the drought year and stopped there. This sentence gives the likely reason for rye's benefit (the soil held moisture), not its effect on corn yield, which is what the goal names.

D.why: You matched the drought year and the yield measurement but not the crop. This is clover's effect, and the goal asks only about cereal rye.
